name: When is cabinet refacing a better option than completely replacing kitchen cabinets?

mainEntity.name: When is cabinet refacing a better option than completely replacing kitchen cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinet refacing is often a better option when your existing cabinet boxes are structurally sound, well-built, and you are satisfied with your kitchen's current layout. If the internal structure of your cabinets is sturdy but the exterior is outdated or damaged, refacing provides a significant aesthetic upgrade without the expense and demolition of a full replacement. A key decision factor is assessing the integrity of your current cabinet frames; if they show signs of water damage, warping, or instability, full replacement might be the more durable long-term solution.
acceptedAnswer.description: Refacing is better when cabinet boxes are sound and the layout is satisfactory. If boxes are damaged or unstable, replacement is a better option.
